citation.title: A comparative study of southern Chinese and British Caucasian cephalometric standards

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08: norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 23 differences (logs/task9a2-compare-<id>.log). Every mean and SD of both extractors re-read from the page images (PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24), and the settled file checked by script against a third, independent reading of the pages (the table in sets.test.ts). Decisions: (0) Source text normalised to one pattern giving table, page, row and column with sex and age (a and b worded it differently; prose only). (1) '1/-A Pog mm' 5 ± 2: a #64 (L1 to A-Pog) / b #63 (U1 to A-Pog) -> #63: the compilation writes the upper incisor '1/' and the lower '/1' (e.g. '/1-MP'); close, incisor point not stated. (2) Y axis, facial axis, gonial angle a same / b close -> close (no definitions in the compilation). Fix round 1 (8 Oct): facial axis -> different, not used (owner FAX-1). Page images: PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24 (Tables I-VI), rendered at 2000 px.

caveats: Quoted second-hand from Moate & Darendeliler 2002 (Aust Orthod J 18:19-26, a compilation of published Chinese cephalometric norms), Table II; the original paper was not read. The compilation rounds every mean and SD to whole numbers (Lew's soft tissue to 0.5) and gives no landmark, plane or method definitions.
The compilation states no film scale or magnification for any study; assumed true size (owner ruling M-2).
120 randomly selected Chinese males aged 12 years, cephalograms in natural head position (text p. 21). Table II prints Cooke under '11 Years'; entered at 11, the table header (merge notes).
'Southern' is from the title; the compilation does not name the place.
Not entered (not catalogue measurements; no ratio computed): S-N (67 ± 3).
Table V (p. 24) averages several studies; it is not entered for this study (merge notes).

entries.definitionNote: Not used (owner ruling 8 Oct): 80–85° with no definition in the compilation; Ricketts' facial axis is 90 ± 3.5, and these values fit Downs' facial angle at least as well — likely a different measurement.

entries.source: Table II, p. 21, row 'Y axis', column Cooke (males, 11 y)
entries.definitionNote: Y axis: definition not stated in the compilation. The catalogue's is Downs' S–Gn to FH (#24). The printed 66° sits about 5° above Zheng 2026's Chinese FH-based Y-axis (60.8–61.1°), which fits S–Gn to SN instead (SN is usually some 6–7° steeper than FH); it cannot be settled from the compilation, so close, not same.
